::: {.callout-important}
Not yet implemented. The manifest schema and hook catalogue are Phase 0 deliverables and exist in
`spec/`; the SDK and the plugin host arrive in Phase 3, and the registry in Phase 9.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Start by not writing a plugin

Most extensions should not be plugins. A script against the [API](api.qmd) or MCP needs no manifest,
no review, no release and no compatibility window, and it cannot take the server down with it. A
complete API removes the need for most plugins, which is the main reason the API is complete.

Write a plugin when you need to take part in a decision the server is in the middle of making. That
is the whole test.
:::

## Four surfaces

| # | Surface | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **API and MCP scripts** | Anything that can happen before or after an operation rather than during it |
| 2 | **Server plugins** | Resolvers, checks, dedup rules, ingest sources and stages, storage backends, importers and exporters, graph edge providers, analytics exports, SR templates |
| 3 | **UI plugins** | Item-pane sections, sidebar panels, context actions, network renderers, screening panels |
| 4 | **Translators** | Zotero's format, belonging upstream in Zotero's translator repository ([ADR-0006](adr.qmd)) |

## Server plugins

An npm package with a `recueil.plugin.json` manifest, validated against
[`spec/plugin-manifest.schema.json`](https://github.com/etabli-dev/etabli-recueil/blob/main/spec/plugin-manifest.schema.json)
at install and at every activation.

```json
{
  "name": "recueil-plugin-example-resolver",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "pluginApi": "^1.0.0",
  "licence": "AGPL-3.0-or-later",
  "permissions": ["network:crossref.org", "items:read", "items:write"],
  "hooks": ["resolver"],
  "settings": { "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema" }
}
```

The manifest declares the plugin API range it works against, the permissions it wants, the hooks it
implements, a JSON Schema for its settings so the UI can render a settings form, and any UI
contributions. **Declare permissions honestly.** v1 runs plugins in-process and trusted, and does
not enforce them by isolation ([ADR-0012](adr.qmd), [ADR-0018](adr.qmd)) — but they are recorded and
shown to the operator at install time, and they become enforceable the moment multi-user exists.

## Hook catalogue (v1)

Hooks let a plugin participate in an operation. Lifecycle events tell it that one happened.

| Hook | Called to |
|---|---|
| `resolver` | Look up metadata by identifier, search by metadata, fetch references, citations or metrics |
| `check` | Contribute a verification check with an id, severity, explanation and optional auto-fix |
| `dedupRule` | Contribute matching or merge logic to either dedup layer |
| `ingestSource` | Feed documents into the pipeline from somewhere new |
| `ingestStage` | Take part in the pipeline itself |
| `storageBackend` | Store and retrieve content-addressed bytes |
| `exporter` / `importer` | Add a serialisation format in either direction |
| `graphEdgeProvider` | Supply graph edges, with provenance |
| `analyticsExport` | Add a table to the Parquet bundle |
| `srTemplate` | Add an extraction form or risk-of-bias instrument |

**Lifecycle events:** `item.created`, `item.updated`, `item.merged`, `item.trashed`,
`item.restored`, `document.ingested`, `attachment.added`, `annotation.created`, `check.completed`,
`job.started`, `job.finished`, `job.failed`.

If what you need is not in this catalogue, the proposal is a request for a new hook rather than a
plugin. New hooks are contract changes and need an ADR. Open an issue describing the workflow you
want to join, not the function you would like to call — the full catalogue with its guarantees is in
[`spec/hooks.md`](https://github.com/etabli-dev/etabli-recueil/blob/main/spec/hooks.md).

## Developer experience

- **`@recueil/plugin-sdk`** — typed. Import this and nothing else from the project. No Drizzle, no
  service classes, no database handle, no direct reach into the content store. An import lint in the
  compatibility suite enforces it, and this is what keeps a future move to a sandboxed host a change
  of host rather than a rewrite of every plugin.
- **`create-recueil-plugin`** — a scaffold with a working example and its tests.
- **Compatibility test suite** — plugins run it in their own CI, against the plugin API version they
  claim.
- **Versioning** — the plugin API is versioned independently of the application, with a
  two-minor-version deprecation window. Before 1.0 it may still break between minors; after 1.0 it
  is frozen at v1.

## First-party plugins

The built-in features are plugins, which is the only reliable way to find out whether the contract
is any good. If a first-party feature needs something the hook catalogue cannot express, the
catalogue is wrong.

`resolver-openalex` · `resolver-crossref` · `resolver-pubmed` · `resolver-s2` · `resolver-datacite` ·
`resolver-isbn` · `checks-core` · `dedup-files` · `dedup-records` · `ingest-imap` · `ingest-webdav` ·
`ingest-folder` · `storage-webdav` · `storage-s3` · `export-bibliometrix` · `export-vosviewer` ·
`export-gephi` · `sr-templates` · `citation-context-scicite`

## Publishing

Name it `recueil-plugin-<something>` on npm; the `@recueil/` scope is reserved for first-party
plugins in the monorepo. Community plugins live in their author's repository at their author's
release pace. The registry is a JSON index in a GitHub repository with install-from-URL support, and
is Phase 9 work; until it exists, link your plugin from a discussion thread.

A plugin that links the server in-process is a derivative work of an AGPL-3.0-or-later program, so
`AGPL-3.0-or-later` is the expected licence for a plugin's own source.

A plugin that duplicates a first-party one is welcome. Competition between a plugin and the built-in
behaviour is a sign the hook is doing its job.
